\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{वाद्यम्} (vādyam)}{वाद्यम् (vādyam)}]{\sk{वाद्यम्} (vādyam) — a musical instrument}

\label{lesson:SA-C121-vadyam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a book, then the Sanskrit for a picture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{वाद्यम्}}
\textbf{\sk{वाद्यम्}} — \emph{vādyam} — \textquotedblleft{}a musical instrument\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vādya} comes from the root √vad \textquotedblleft{}speak, sound\textquotedblright{}: first \textquotedblleft{}to be said\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}to be played\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}a musical instrument\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11511). It lives on as Hindi \emph{bājā} \textquotedblleft{}musical instrument\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11511).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vādyam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{vādyam}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a book, then the Sanskrit for a picture, then say \emph{vādyam} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{वीणा} (vīṇā)}{वीणा (vīṇā)}]{\sk{वीणा} (vīṇā) — a veena}

\label{lesson:SA-C121-vina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a picture, then the Sanskrit for a musical instrument.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{वीणा}}
\textbf{\sk{वीणा}} — \emph{vīṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}a veena\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
MW calls \emph{vīṇā} \textquotedblleft{}the Indian lute\textquotedblright{} of doubtful derivation; EtymDB traces it to an Indo-Iranian word that Middle Persian also kept, so its source is not settled. It lives on as Hindi \emph{bīn} \textquotedblleft{}lute\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12048).
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{पट्टः} (paṭṭaḥ)}{पट्टः (paṭṭaḥ)}]{\sk{पट्टः} (paṭṭaḥ) — a cloth, a strip}

\label{lesson:SA-C121-pattah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a musical instrument, then the Sanskrit for a veena.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पट्टः}}
\textbf{\sk{पट्टः}} — \emph{paṭṭaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a cloth, a strip\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{paṭṭa} \textquotedblleft{}cloth, woven silk, a strip or bandage\textquotedblright{} is probably from a non-Aryan source, says CDIAL 7700, which rejects a link with \emph{pattra} \textquotedblleft{}leaf\textquotedblright{}. It lives on as Hindi \emph{paṭṭī} \textquotedblleft{}strip of cloth\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7700).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{रत्नम्} (ratnam)}{रत्नम् (ratnam)}]{\sk{रत्नम्} (ratnam) — a jewel}

\label{lesson:SA-C121-ratnam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a veena, then the Sanskrit for a cloth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{रत्नम्}}
\textbf{\sk{रत्नम्}} — \emph{ratnam} — \textquotedblleft{}a jewel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ratna} first meant \textquotedblleft{}a gift, wealth\textquotedblright{} in the Rigveda and later \textquotedblleft{}a jewel\textquotedblright{} (MW). MW derives it from the root √rā \textquotedblleft{}give\textquotedblright{}, while CDIAL 10600 refers it to √raṇ \textquotedblleft{}rejoice\textquotedblright{}, so its root is not settled. Pali kept it as \emph{ratana} \textquotedblleft{}jewel\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10600).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सुवर्णम्} (suvarṇam)}{सुवर्णम् (suvarṇam)}]{\sk{सुवर्णम्} (suvarṇam) — gold}

\label{lesson:SA-C121-suvarnam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a cloth, then the Sanskrit for a jewel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सुवर्णम्}}
\textbf{\sk{सुवर्णम्}} — \emph{suvarṇam} — \textquotedblleft{}gold\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{suvarṇa} is built from \emph{su} \textquotedblleft{}good\textquotedblright{} and \emph{varṇa} \textquotedblleft{}colour\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13519): \textquotedblleft{}of a good, bright colour\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}gold\textquotedblright{}. It wore down into Hindi, Punjabi and Bengali \emph{sonā} \textquotedblleft{}gold\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13519).
\end{cousinweb}
